cards.title: Introduction to Web Basics
cards.content: As a Flask developer, understanding how the web works is crucial. Flask is a Python web framework that handles HTTP requests and returns HTTP responses.

cards.title: HTTP Methods
cards.content:
Clients communicate with servers using HTTP methods:

  • GET: Retrieve data
  • POST: Submit data
  • PUT: Update data
  • DELETE: Remove data

options.text: GET is used to submit new data to the server securely.
GET is used to request data from a specified resource.
GET is used to delete records from a database.

content.text: To create a route in Flask that listens for POST requests, we use the methods parameter: @app.route('/submit', _____=['POST'])

steps: Client enters URL and sends HTTP Request
Web server receives request and forwards to WSGI gateway
Flask matches URL to a view function
Flask processes logic and returns HTTP Response

cards.title: Client-Server Architecture Summary
cards.content: In a Flask application, the browser acts as the Client, and your Python application running via Werkzeug/Gunicorn acts as the Server. They talk entirely through HTTP.
